newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts head up after U.S. bond rally, eye pound.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts head up after U.S. bond rally, eye pound.

text.p: 0710 GMT - UK gilt futures moved ahead in early trade inspired by overnight gains in U.S. Treasuries but dealers said a further retreat by sterling was hampering sentiment. UK June consumer credit data due at 0830 GMT, US employment cost due 1230 GMT key.*LIFFE Sept gilts up 6/32 at 115-12/32

The pound was down more than one pfennig from late Monday levels at 3.0008/13 marks but was above the early lows of around 2.9900. Savage profit-taking sent the British currency down by around two percent on Monday as dealers began to speculate that the Bank of England might not increase official interest rates next week.
UK consumer credit data for June are due at 0830 GMT and the Reuter consensus forecasts is of a 1.0 billion stg rise but Royal Bank of Scotland economist Neil Parker sees a rise of 950 million stg.

"This should support gilts and short sterling and could undermine sterling. If consumer credit is weaker the monetary policy committee (MPC) could find it harder to justify a fourth rise in succession since the election," he said.
British interest rates have risen three times since the election with base rates now standing at 6.75 percent. the Bank of England's rate setting MPC is due to meet on August 6 and 7.

At the short end of the yield curve, short sterling continues to discount a rate rise of 25 basis points over the next two months. By 0740 GMT, the September contract was unchanged at 92.78 whilst the more active December contract was up one basis point at 92.63.

The main focus for bond markets internationally is the U.S. second quarter employment cost index due at 1230 GMT, with the consensus forecast at up 0.8 percent quarter on quarter, suggesting a stable U.S. inflation environment.
Dealers expect the figures to give another boost to Treasuries and for gilts to be dragged higher accordingly.
Gilts were suffering relative to Bunds because of the pound's weakening. The 10 year gilt/Bund spread widened to 155 basis points from Monday's closing level of 153.
